2608.26191.title: Structured Evidence Routing for Incident Risk Prediction from Multimodal Longitudinal EHRs
2608.26191.paper_summary: Incident risk prediction from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) is challenging because relevant signals are multimodal, weak in isolation, and distributed across irregular patient histories. We propose structured evidence routing, a router-predictor-reviewer workflow that separates full-record access from disease-specific assessment. The router organizes the complete pre-index EHR into a compact summary and targeted evidence slices; the predictor uses this evidence to form an evidence-linked risk assessment, which the reviewer critiques. For comparison with supervised EHRSHOT baselines, we pair the routed evidence summaries with a supervised classifier readout. Across five 1-year incident diagnosis tasks, our method reaches the AUROC range of established supervised EHRSHOT baselines and remains competitive on AUPRC, while exposing a patient-specific evidence trail. Internal pre-readout ablations further suggest that routing, laboratory evidence, task guidance, and review each contribute to performance.
2608.26191.paper_summary_zh: 從縱向電子健康記錄 (EHRs) 預測事件風險是具有挑戰性的，因為相關信號是多模態的、孤立時較弱，且分佈在不規則的病歷中。<lb/>我們提出了結構化證據路由，一種將完整記錄訪問與特定疾病評估分開的路由器-預測器-審查者工作流程。<lb/>路由器將完整的預索引 EHR 組織成一個緊湊的摘要和針對性的證據切片；預測器使用這些證據形成一個與證據相關的風險評估，審查者對此進行評析。<lb/>為了與監督式 EHRSHOT 基準進行比較，我們將路由的證據摘要與監督式分類器的讀出配對。<lb/>在五個一年期的事件診斷任務中，我們的方法達到了已建立的監督式 EHRSHOT 基準的 AUROC 範圍，並在 AUPRC 上保持競爭力，同時揭示了特定患者的證據軌跡。<lb/>內部預讀出消融進一步表明，路由、實驗室證據、任務指導和審查各自對性能有所貢獻。
